correctness.rationale: The exact finite signed-incidence component rank identity was reconstructed and checked exhaustively for 5,018 cases. Joint factorial moments give independent short-cycle Poisson limits; bicyclic components and long cycles vanish for c<1; independent sign thinning yields the logarithmic Poisson parameter, and a column-coupling argument gives divergence for c>=1. A verifier covered finite tests but did not substitute for the analytical proof.

originality.rationale: The claimed contribution is the correlation-dependent full distribution of SparseStack column nullity and sharp threshold at two-block density one, not the classical incidence-matroid identity or Poisson sparse-cycle count. Accessible references provide the sketch construction and general embedding/full-rank theory but do not imply the exact two-parameter Poisson law in the degree-two bipartite model. Semantic records searches returned no equivalent finding. A close older signed-graph application or inaccessible primary full text could change the priority judgment.

value.rationale: Two-stack sparse sketches are used to preserve subspace information at minimal per-column sampling cost. Their injectivity failure probability for coherent coordinate subspaces is a nontrivial, nonvanishing limiting operational reliability risk. The correlation parameter quantifies the cost of reusing sign bits, while the complete Poisson law and sharp critical density distinguish structural failure from mere expected distortion. Rank failure itself invalidates every OSE guarantee on this subspace.
